definition: GraphiCon is the largest International conference on computer graphics and computer vision in the countries of the former Soviet Union.
details: Established in 1991. The conference is hosted by Moscow State University in association with Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics, Russian Center of Computing for Physics and Technology, and the Russian Computer Graphics Society. The Conference is held in close cooperation with Eurographics Association.

explainer.lead: GraphiCon is an international conference for computer graphics and computer vision, established in 1991. It is the largest conference covering these subjects in the countries of the former Soviet Union, giving researchers and practitioners a shared place to present and discuss their work.

tiers.eli5: GraphiCon is like a big show-and-tell for people who teach computers to make pictures or understand what they see. It began in 1991 and brings together work on computer graphics and computer vision. Several scientific organizations help run it, and it works closely with an international graphics association.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers working in graphics or vision, GraphiCon is a conference setting for presenting and discussing technical work rather than a software tool or dataset. Its scope covers both creating visual content with computers and interpreting visual information. Its international character should not be confused with a restriction to participants from the former Soviet Union.
tiers.paperLevel: GraphiCon can be described formally as an international conference whose subject scope is computer graphics and computer vision, established in 1991. It is hosted by Moscow State University with three associated Russian organizations and held in close cooperation with the Eurographics Association. Its defining regional distinction is being the largest such conference in the countries of the former Soviet Union.

explainer.example: A researcher with work in computer graphics or computer vision could use GraphiCon as the conference setting for presenting and discussing that work with an international audience, within an event hosted by Moscow State University and supported by its partner organizations.

usedIn.name: Computer graphics
usedIn.detail: One of GraphiCon's two main subject areas, concerned with creating and processing visual content with computers.

usedIn.name: Computer vision
usedIn.detail: The conference's other main subject area, concerned with enabling computers to interpret visual information.

usedIn.name: International scientific exchange
usedIn.detail: The conference connects its regional hosting institutions with an international scope and cooperation with Eurographics.

explainer.outcome: GraphiCon became the largest international conference on computer graphics and computer vision in the countries of the former Soviet Union. Its organization combines a university host, specialist Russian institutions, and cooperation with an international graphics association.
explainer.whyItMatters: GraphiCon provides a major regional meeting point with an international scope for two closely related computing fields. Its institutional partnerships connect computer graphics and vision work across academic and specialist organizations.
